---
title: "Naming rules (draft)"
description: "The draft rules for DataSHIELD function, test file and argument names."
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Draft
Nothing here is agreed with the DataSHIELD developers yet. Where a rule
lists several options, it is still open: the first one is used for now,
and renames that depend on it are marked `rule_open: true`.
:::

The rules are in two files of this repository, used by the
[naming workflows](ds-naming.qmd):

| File | Rules for |
|---|---|
| `config/ds-naming-package-rules.yml` | Packages in general: package names, function names, server methods, test file names |
| `config/ds-naming-argument-rules.yml` | Function arguments: style, classes, roles and order |

## Package rules

These are reported by the check; the apply workflow doesn't change them.

### Package names

A pair is called `ds<name>` (server) and `ds<name>Client` (client), where
`<name>` is camelCase and starts with a capital letter: `dsBase` and
`dsBaseClient`.

Exceptions are listed in the rules:

- **Client only:** dsHelper, dsSyntheticClient;
- **Server only:** dsResource, dsMeta;
- **Pairs named differently:** dsMTLClient and dsMTLBase.

A package that isn't listed, and is checked without its counterpart, is
reported.

### Function names

| Side | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Client | `ds.` + camelCase | `ds.mean` |
| Server | ends in `DS`, digits go before it | `meanDS`, `glm1DS` |

Open: the prefixes `dh.` and `dss`, and the forms `ds.vert.` and
`ds.imaging.`, count as following the rules for now.

### Server methods

A server package declares its Aggregate and Assign methods in
`inst/DATASHIELD`, not in `DESCRIPTION`, as packages on CRAN do:

```
AssignMethods:
    selectDS,
    renameDS
AggregateMethods:
    groupKeysDS
```

Every declared method has a function behind it, unless it points to
another package (`asChar=base::as.character`).

### Client and server

These go by the calls a client package actually makes, not by comparing
names: one client function can call several server functions, and some
call none.

- Every server method a client function calls is declared by the server
  package.
- Every declared method is called by a client function.

Client calls are recognised in `call("meanDS", …)`,
`paste0("meanDS(", …)` and strings passed directly to `datashield.aggregate()`
or `datashield.assign()`. A method called in another way is listed as not
called.

### Test file names {#test-files}

Test files in `tests/testthat/` follow the template

```
^test-(<category>-)?<function>(-<variant>)?\.R$
```

where `(…)?` means optional. For
`test-smk_expt-ds.mean-factor_missing.R`:

| Template part | Matches | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `^test-` | `test-` | fixed start |
| `(<category>-)?` | `smk_expt-` | categories `smk` and `expt`, joined by `_`; optional |
| `<function>` | `ds.mean` | the function being tested, following the [function name](#function-names) rule of the package's side |
| `(-<variant>)?` | `-factor_missing` | free-text variant; optional |
| `\.R$` | `.R` | fixed end |

The categories are `smk`, `arg`, `perf`, `disc`, `discctrl`, `datachk`,
`expt`, `math` and `dgr`. The qualifier `bug` can follow a category.

These names also pass:

| File name | Category | Function | Variant |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test-ds.mean.R` | none | `ds.mean` | none |
| `test-smk-ds.mean.R` | `smk` | `ds.mean` | none |
| `test-expt_bug-ds.table.R` | `expt` + qualifier `bug` | `ds.table` | none |
| `test-ds.mean-factor_missing.R` | none | `ds.mean` | `factor_missing` |

These fail:

| File name | Why |
|---|---|
| `test-bug-ds.mean.R` | `bug` is a qualifier, so it can only follow a category |
| `test-ds.mean.r` | the ending must be `.R` |
| `test-smk-ds.mean-Factor.R` | a variant can only use lowercase letters, digits and `_` |
| `ds.mean.R` | the `test-` start is missing |

The template only checks the shape of the name. A second step checks that
it names a function of the package: `test-smk-ds.typo.R` matches the
template but is reported if `ds.typo` doesn't exist. Test files of internal
functions, or of functions under the open prefixes, are reported too.
`setup.R`, `teardown.R` and
`helper-*.R` are exempt.

## Argument rules

An argument's name depends on what it is. Client arguments usually hold
the *name* of something on the server, so a name says what it refers to,
without a `.name` suffix: `df`, not `df.name`.

### Roles

Roles apply whatever the argument's class is.

| Role | Name | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| Connection | `datasources` | The connections from `datashield.login()` |
| New object | `newobj` | The name for the result on the server |
| Output type | `type` | `split`, `combine` or `both` |
| Checks | `checks` or `classConsistencyCheck` (open) | The switch for optional pre-checks |
| Method | `method` | The choice of algorithm or variant |
| Seed | `seed` | The seed for random numbers on the server |

### Object classes

For an argument naming an object on the server:

| Class | Name |
|---|---|
| Vector | `x` |
| Data frame | `df` |
| Matrix | `mat` or `matrix` (open) |
| Tibble | `tbl` |
| Model | `model` |
| Formula | `formula` |
| List | `lst` or `x` (open) |
| Omics object | `set`, `eset` or `x` (open) |
| Resource | `resource` or `res` (open) |

### Columns and values

- **A column inside a data frame** gets the suffix `.col` or `_col` (open),
  `.cols` / `_cols` for several: `idCol` → `id.col`.
- **A plain value** sent from the client, such as a threshold, keeps its
  name in the general style.

### Style

- **Words** are separated by `.` or `_` (open), in lower case.
- **Too generic names** go to Claude for a closer look, as they say little
  about the argument: `matrix`, `tibble`, `data`, `object`, `what`, `input`.
- **R conventions** keep their name: `...`, `formula`, `family`, `weights`,
  `offset`, `na.rm`, `subset`.

### Several inputs of the same class

Numbered (`df1`, `df2`) or distinct (`x`, `y`) is open; numbered is used
for now. Established `x`, `y` pairs stay, e.g. in `ds.cor` and `ds.cov`.
Descriptive names such as `sex` are kept.

### Order

`datasources` comes last; only `...` may follow it. This is reported by
the check; the apply workflow doesn't reorder arguments.

### Exceptions

- **dsTidyverse and dsTidyverseClient** mirror dplyr's argument names.
- **Protocol arguments** such as `session_id` keep their names.
- **The server suffix `.transmit`** stays on arguments that have it (open).
